newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica resort has $7 million in damages from fire.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica resort has $7 million in damages from fire.

text.p: The owners of the popular Half Moon Resort in Montego Bay, Jamaica, were assessing their losses Monday after a weekend fire that caused an estimated $7 million in damages and forced the relocation of almost 200 guests.

Local fire officials said the blaze began at about 9:00 a.m. EST (1400 GMT) Sunday morning in the resort's kitchen when an oven caught fire. Within an hour, the main lobby and nearby shops were ablaze as well.

Six units from nearby fire stations were called out, but low water pressure forced firefighters to pump water directly from the sea. Eight rooms were destroyed and another 50 affected by the fire. Of the 586 registered guests, 197 have been relocated elsewhere on the property or to nearby hotels, hotel managers said.
The resort is owned by Heinz Simonitsch, an Austrian businessman who resides in Jamaica.
